title: ban-reason.ts handleBanReasonModal: reason length check is untrimmed, so a whitespace-only reason is stored
reason: ban-reason.ts:103 checks `reason.length < 10` (cited :267 is isBanReasonModal). Modal min_length 10 (ban-confirmation.ts:104) counts spaces, and extractTextInputValue does not trim. The value reaches banUser (:171), which binds it to banned_users.reason and moderation_log (ban-service.ts:498-507). Rejection/revert use reason.trim().length (preset-rejection.ts:121,240). The actor is a trusted moderator.

This is a decided trade-off. CLAUDE.md (Localization) and bot-i18n.ts:160-162 keep the locale resolution on purpose, and the dead-code audit's DEAD-027 explicitly keeps getLocale as an accepted observation hook. The gain is negligible: at most 2 edge-cached KV gets on a rate-limited, moderator-only command path. Origin is also MAIN (I18N-009 commit 0e5e5ea9 is on main), not PR-#225.

The claimed failure cannot happen. Types are erased and the same parsed object (index.ts:173) reaches editReviewMessage unchanged, since no code copies interaction fields. Dropping `flags` from any declared type cannot remove it at runtime, and reading it through a type that lacks it would be a tsc error, not a silent miss. Duplicate interface declarations inside one app, with no correctness risk, fall below the brief's REFACTOR bar.

Unreachable. The bot cannot load a PENDING preset to edit it: lookupPreset calls getPreset with no user id, so canSeePreset returns 404 and the bot replies 'not found'. Name lookup filters to approved. The web app posts nothing of its own. The approved-to-pending path passes the flagged_edit cap and is the duplicate counted in -02.

title: presets-api webhook + discord-worker bot-side posts both fire for bot submissions/edits -> duplicate moderation and submission-log embeds
reason: presets-api fires the webhook for every created row, with no source filter. discord-worker's webhook posts pending presets to MODERATION_CHANNEL_ID and approved ones to SUBMISSION_LOG_CHANNEL_ID. After that response the bot posts again (notifySubmissionChannel / notifyModerationChannel, legacy ids). Approved-preset bot edits whose text gets flagged double the same way through notifyEditModerationChannel.

Moderator-only and defended by the one moderator client: refreshed embeds offer buttons only for pending presets, and both the approve command and the approve button refuse a banned author's preset. On main the status route already bound to the stored status, so hidden->approved was always a moderator's deliberate manual restore.

title: presets PATCH/POST and moderation status/revert: JSON body `null` -> TypeError -> opaque 500 instead of 400
reason: jsonDepthLimit lets a non-object through (structure.ts:40-41 returns null for scalars and null). c.req.json() of 'null' yields null, and `!body.name` / validateSubmission's body.name / body.status then throw TypeError. The global onError answers 500 instead of 400.

title: presets PATCH /:id re-moderates unchanged text; a failing/unscored verdict re-queues an approved (or resubmits a rejected) preset
reason: The text_edit reservation and moderateContent are gated on `body.name || body.description`, not on textChanged. When stored text fails or is unscored (moderator-approved-after-flag text, Perspective outage, every call after the key sunset), re-sending it unchanged sets flaggedByThisEdit. ownerEditOutcome then moves an approved or rejected preset to pending and notifies. The existing 'unchanged' test only exercises text that passes moderation.

Moderator-only route. Its only client, the moderation-worker reject modal, always sends a 10-500 character string, and the 100 KB body cap bounds the rest. A non-string or oversized reason needs a trusted moderator to hand-craft a request. Worth hardening, but not a defect.

Speculative. The candidate itself says 'fine today'. Categories are ~10 and the count query runs at most once per 60s edge-cache window per isolate, deduped in flight. No benchmark shows a gain at current preset volume.

title: presets-api webhook + discord-worker /preset submit/edit both post the same submission to the moderation/submission-log channels
reason: presets-api posts a webhook on every submit and edit with no check on authSource (presets.ts:1077 for submit, ~853 for edit), and the bot's command handler also posts to the same channels (preset.ts:571/576/924). sendModerationNotification has no idempotency guard, so a bot submission or edit produces two posts.

title: validation-service validatePresetDyes accepts repeated dye ids, bypassing the 3-dye floor and dye_signature dedup
reason: validatePresetDyes (validation-service.ts:236-256) checks count, integer and range but never uniqueness, so [x,x,x] and [1,2,3,3] get distinct sorted signatures. A real path exists: /preset submit dye1..dye3 can all name the same dye, and a clean result is auto-approved.

title: validation-service name/description min-length counts whitespace; whitespace-only values pass
reason: The length checks at validation-service.ts:182/208 run on the raw string, and presets-api never trims name or description, so '  ' passes and is stored blank. The web form trims (preset-submission-form.ts:679), so only direct API callers hit this: LOW.

title: validation-service validateExampleLink rejects a leading-space link that normalizeExampleLink would accept
reason: validateExampleLink does not trim (validation-service.ts:438). With a leading space the scheme regex fails and it prefixes 'https://'; node shows new URL('https:// https://x.com/a') throws, giving a 400, although normalizeExampleLink trims. Both first-party clients are defended (the web form trims, the bot has no link option): LOW.

title: preset-service getPresets ORDER BY lacks unique tiebreaker
reason: LIMIT and OFFSET are bound parameters, so every page runs the same plan and SQLite (which D1 is) orders ties deterministically. A node:sqlite probe of the real COUNT(*) OVER() query with 150-row tie groups across page boundaries gave 0 repeats or skips. Drift from concurrent writes is inherent to OFFSET pagination, and an id tiebreaker would not fix it.

title: identity-rekey-service rekeyIdentity(db,id,id) silently wipes the user's votes; no self-guard or test
reason: With fromId===toId, statement 2 moves nothing, so statement 3 decrements vote_count for every vote the user has and statement 4 deletes all of their votes (identity-rekey-service.ts:39-62). The only caller guards it (presets.ts:372-374, jwtSub !== jwtDiscordId) and no test covers equal ids, so this is latent: LOW.

title: rate-limit-service lazy prune per write despite daily cron
reason: Decided trade-off: the retention-job.ts header says the lazy write-path prunes stay because they keep working on a worker with no cron, and the cron is production-only ([env.production.triggers]). The gain is one DELETE on writes capped at a few per user per day. The origin is also wrong: the lazy prune is MAIN (rate-limit-service.ts:188,292 at 8ecb878f).

title: index.ts telemetry limiter registered twice; each beacon is charged 2x against the 240/60s fail-closed bucket
reason: index.ts:128-129 registers telemetryRateLimitMiddleware on both TELEMETRY_PATH and `${TELEMETRY_PATH}/*`. A temporary repro that drove the real index.ts app (since deleted) recorded 2 limit() calls ['telemetry:ip:203.0.113.9:t240_60' x2] for one POST /v1/telemetry and 1 call for /v1/telemetry/x. The bucket fails closed, so the effective cap is 120 beacons per IP, not 240.

title: parseIntParam/parseFloatParam accept trailing garbage and exponent forms in query params
reason: validation.ts:202 uses parseInt and :244 uses parseFloat with only NaN/finite guards. The repro gave parseIntParam('1e2')=1, '2abc'=2, '50.9'=50, ' 7'=7 and parseFloatParam('10px')=10. Callers are match.ts:78/80, dyes.ts:277-290, harmony.ts:99 and wheels.ts:42. Only the icon id has the CANONICAL guard (chara/router.ts:273).

title: XIVAPI_VERSION="latest" makes the chara row-cache namespace constant, so a patch never cold-starts the cache
reason: Both envs set XIVAPI_VERSION="latest" (wrangler.toml:47 and :113), and CharaRowCache's prefix is `chara:3:${client.versionKey}`, the literal env string (cache.ts:41, router.ts:203). The namespace never changes across patches, so the 'roll forward = cold cache' design (cache.ts:5-7) cannot happen and rows (including cached-empty 'no item row') persist up to TTL+SWR. The claim that `latest` 503s during ingest is unverified.

title: chara acquisition/ko/zh JSON tables (3.4 MB raw) are evaluated at isolate start for every route
reason: acquisition.ts:11 and regional-names.ts:16-17 statically import 1.36 MB + 1.10 MB + 0.90 MB of JSON. The chain index.ts -> chara/router.ts:27 -> resolver.ts:36-37 is eager, so every isolate builds these objects at startup, including for /health, /v1/dyes and /universalis. The gain is unmeasured and likely small, so it is LOW.

title: ko/zh item-name tables older than acquisition table (documented lag, EN fallback)
reason: This is a documented, decided trade-off. regional-names.ts:10-13 says the tables can lag and a missing item falls back to EN. Both scripts use the same EquipSlotCategory!=0 filter but different sources (a local datamining Item.csv vs XIVAPI), and the KR/CN clients trail global. Nothing shows that regenerating would produce names for the ~65 new items.

title: apps/oauth/src/index.ts /auth/* limiter keys and tiers on the raw percent-encoded pathname, while Hono routes on the decoded path
reason: Line 184 is `new URL(c.req.url).pathname` (raw). hono 4.13.9 getPath decodeURIs, so /auth/%63allback still routes to the callback handler, but getOAuthLimit's startsWith misses and returns the default 30/min, and every spelling gets its own bucket. Reproduced via app.fetch: 25 POSTs to /auth/%63allback all got 400 'Missing code' with X-RateLimit-Limit 30 and no 429. The literal path returned 429 from request 21. Caveat: Cloudflare zone URL normalization could decode %63 before the Worker sees it. That setting is not in the repo, so the grade stays MEDIUM, not HIGH.

title: POST /auth/callback and /auth/xivauth/callback destructure a null JSON body outside the parse try, giving a 500 instead of a 400
reason: c.req.json() on body `null` succeeds and returns null, and jsonDepthLimit's validateStructure(null) returns ok. `const { code, ... } = body` (callback.ts:64, xivauth.ts:95) then throws, and app.onError returns 500. Reproduced: both endpoints returned 500 'Cannot destructure property code of body as it is null'. Error shape only, no data impact.

title: xivauth.ts roster guard (BUG-051) validates only that the roster is an array; a null element gives a 500, and an empty verified name gives an empty username
reason: characters = roster when it is an array (line 297), so with [null] the filter throws inside the try and `characters` stays [null]. Then find at :342 throws outside it, giving 500 'Authentication failed'. Reproduced. A verified character with name '' passes `??` and produced a 200 with an empty display name. Latent: it needs the trusted XIVAuth upstream to return malformed data.

title: oauth tests never send a percent-encoded /auth path through the app's limiter or a JSON `null` body to the POST callbacks
reason: A grep of apps/oauth/src/__tests__ for %XX path escapes or a 'null' body finds only one unrelated redirect_uri assertion (callback.test.ts:960). The rate-limit tests call checkRateLimit with literal paths, and the invalid-body tests send malformed JSON only. That is how oauth-01 and oauth-02 went unnoticed.

title: gradient.ts generateGradientOG ranks middle-band dyes by hardcoded 'ciede2000' while printing the delta and footer in the requested algo
reason: Real. The crawler emits ?algo= on gradient image URLs and the page ranks by that method, but the card picks DE2000-nearest dyes and labels them in the other unit. The repro showed 17/30 pairs differ. Edge path (non-default algo only), so MEDIUM.

title: harmony.ts passes a raw legacy ?algo= (hyab/euclidean/oklch-weighted) to core generateHarmonySlots; getDistanceForMethod returns undefined and the card shows dyes in table order
reason: The wrong output is real and shown by the repro. Graded LOW, not MEDIUM: since f3ad612c (2026-08-18) the only producer, withAlgo, normalises before emitting, so only a hand-built image URL reaches it.

title: gradient.test.ts has no algorithm case; harmony.test.ts:233 lists only the six 5.0 spellings and asserts only '<svg'
reason: Accurate. No test pins gradient ranking by algorithm or harmony with legacy spellings, which is why -01 and -02 ship green.

title: index.ts ogCacheKey keys algo and mode on every /og route although only 5 routes read algo and 2 read mode, contradicting its own docblock
reason: Real but bounded: the guard caps it at about 10 algo x mode states per path. Ruling S7-R7 accepted that bound before BUG-018 set the stricter rule now stated in the docblock. Operational waste only.

title: extractor.ts matches by hardcoded ciede2000 and the crawler forwards algo only onto og:url, so the unfurl can name different dyes than the page
reason: Real divergence from the project rule that a card previews the page (harmony.ts:89-95). The card is honest about its algorithm and only a non-default algo diverges, so LOW. No decision record exempts extractor.

title: renderer.ts renderSvgToPng never .free()s Resvg or RenderedImage, leaving each render's wasm allocations to FinalizationRegistry timing
reason: The missing free() is factual and the fix is two lines. The memory-pressure impact is unmeasured: no OOM has been observed and finalisation does eventually run. Hence OPT with LOW impact, not a BUG.

title: stoat dye-resolver.ts resolveDyeInputMulti: step 1 resolveColorInput first-match makes multiple/disambiguation unreachable for name queries
reason: resolveColorInput's name step is a substring search (searchByName includes) that returns candidates[0], so dye-resolver.ts:54-56 answers 'single' for every name substring. Repro: 'white' gives single Snow White (4 hits), 'Red' gives Rolanberry Red (11 hits); 'multiple'/'disambiguation' only happen for category-only queries ('neutral').

title: stoat dye-resolver.ts ignores locale and initializeLocale is never called, while help advertises localized names
reason: _locale is unused (dye-resolver.ts:46) and stoat never calls initializeLocale. info.ts:38 also hard-codes 'en'. help.ts advertises localized names (:28) and gives スノウホワイト as an example (:49); the repro returns kind 'none' for it and for 'Schneeweiß'.

title: stoat about.ts Quick Start advertises unrouted !xd random and an unimplemented ❓-reaction help
reason: about.ts:23 advertises '!xd random'. parser.ts:60 aliases it to dye.random, which is not in COMMAND_ROUTES (router.ts:101-109), so the reply is 'Unknown command "dye.random"'. about.ts:25 also advertises a ❓-reaction help that has no listener (BUG-038 design).

title: image-worker /extract null JSON body -> 500
reason: Unreachable input. image-worker has workers_dev=false and no routes (wrangler.toml:24,42), plus a .workers.dev 404 guard. Its only /extract caller (discord-worker image-client.ts:48-57) always sends JSON.stringify of an object with a url, so a 'null' body cannot arrive.

title: photon.ts resizeImage no-resize copy via PNG encode/decode
reason: No current path pays the cost, so the expected gain is zero. resizeImage is called only from processImageForExtraction (/extract); /thumbnail does not use it. The only caller (extractor.ts:507) passes no maxDimension, so the bound is 256, and only images of 256 px or less take the get_bytes copy.

title: stoat dye-resolver.test.ts multiple/disambiguation tests cannot fail (any-kind else / guarded if)
reason: dye-resolver.test.ts:83-114 and :181-190 accept any of the three kinds, or guard their checks in an if with no else, so they cannot fail. The repro shows 'Coral' and 'Blue' resolve as single while these tests pass. The partial test mocks resolveColorInput to null (partial.test.ts:12-16), forcing a branch the real code never takes.

title: MessageContextStore.set evicts on overwrite at capacity
reason: Unreachable input. The only writer is info.ts:124, keyed by the fresh bot-reply id (sent.id), so set() never sees an existing key. get/delete/size have no production reader (DEAD-064, KEEP), so a wrong eviction has no observable effect.

title: blending.ts blendHSL interpolates the hue of an achromatic input, which is meaningless (always 0), so grey/white/black mixes get a hue neither input has
reason: rgbToHsl returns h:0 for any grey (conversions.ts:240-242), and blendHSL interpolates it as a real hue. Measured: white+blue at 0.5 in hsl mode gives #DF9FDF (pink), not light blue; black+green gives #606020 (olive, hue 60). Reachable in the web mixer, bot /mixer and /gradient hsl modes.

title: HarmonySelector.generateHarmonySlots reserves a pinned dye only for later slots under preventDuplicates, so an earlier slot can choose the same dye
reason: `used` starts empty and a pin enters it only when its own slot is reached (:242-258), so an earlier unpinned slot can still pick it. Measured: triadic on Dalamud Red with slot 1 pinned to slot 0's pick gives ['Cactuar Green','Cactuar Green']. The claim's exact path (picking the dye from slot 2's companion list) is not reachable, because those companions already exclude earlier dyes. It is reachable because harmony-tool keeps swappedDyes across method, companion-count, dedup and filter changes: switching cie76->ciede2000 after a pin duplicated in 3 base x type combos.

title: HarmonySelector.test.ts pin test pins Jet Black, a dye no earlier slot picks, so it cannot detect the earlier-slot duplicate
reason: The test pins slot 1 of a Dalamud Red triadic to Jet Black, which slot 0 never chooses. Its `toHaveLength(1)` uniqueness assertion therefore passes regardless of order, while core-color-02 shows the bug when the pin equals slot 0's natural pick.

title: ColorAccessibility.isLightColor/getOptimalTextColor use a luminance threshold of 0.5, which picks the lower-contrast text for luminance between about 0.18 and 0.5
reason: For #FF8000 (L about 0.367), isLightColor returns false, so the text is white at about 2.5:1 while black gives about 8.3:1. This is published ColorService API with no in-repo caller: web-app budget-tool has its own private isLightColor. DEAD-048 is KEEP, not REMOVE, so the candidate is not superseded. LOW because it is latent.

title: blendColors lets a NaN ratio through Math.max/Math.min and returns the invalid hex '#NaNNaNNaN'
reason: Real only on the direct blendColors path (/blending export): measured '#NaNNaNNaN' for both rgb and lab. The stated ColorService.mixColorsRgb repro is wrong: fromBlend -> ColorConverter.rgbToHex throws a typed AppError. Every in-repo direct caller passes a finite ratio, so the bug is latent.

title: ColorConverter.hsvToRgb caches under a key rounded to 2 dp but stores the result computed from the unrounded inputs, so the output depends on call order
reason: Measured: hsvToRgb(0,50.004,100) then hsvToRgb(0,49.996,100) returns {255,127,127} for the second call, while a fresh instance gives {255,128,128}. Live through hsvToHex in the web gradient tool and the bot /gradient. Off by one unit per channel, so cosmetic.

Not a wrong result. Both branches of findComplementaryPair anchor on the caller's own colour, so the method is self-consistent, and complementing the actual input is defensible. The colorSpace option is @deprecated (DyeService.ts:214, HarmonyGenerator.ts:121), and the find* family has no in-repo caller (DEAD-047 KEEP).

title: chara-parser readModelLane: an out-of-range lane (>65535) sinks the whole /v1/chara/resolve batch
reason: readModelLane (chara-parser.ts:498) floors any positive finite value with no upper bound; api-worker router.ts:73 400s the whole body on any lane > LANE_MAX, and chara-resolve-service.ts:147 turns any non-ok into CharaResolveUnavailableError, so every piece in the file loses its name.

title: chara-parser parseFloatColor accepts empty segments as 0 (and Infinity), producing a silent wrong lip/colour
reason: chara-parser.ts:237 maps Number('') to 0, so "0.2,0.3,0.4," passes the NaN check as 4 parts with alpha 0 and resolver :345 marks the lip inert/noLip; this contradicts the function's own doc promise to throw loudly on malformed values. Hand-edit only.

Defended by design: a chunk-load rejection is a loud, retryable failure, the same contract as the hair/skin sheet dynamic imports awaited in the same resolve (CharacterColorService.ts:175,202; resolver :305,:365). chara-file-loader.ts:66-77 catches it and returns a localized 'failed' result; the loader's cache resets so a retry works. No wrong value is shown.

This is the designed unknown-stain path: getByStainId returns null and the UI and GPOSERS show the file's own value as '#id' (chara-gposers.ts:44 'or `#id` for a stain the build does not know'; glamour-block.ts:789,844). Flooring 1.5 to 1 would invent a dye. Only a hand edit reaches it, and nothing crashes.

title: CharacterColorService.findClosestDyes BUG-056 guard misses NaN/non-number count -> TypeError on best[-1]
reason: StorageService.getItem returns the raw string when JSON.parse fails (storage-service.ts:81-83), so a corrupted v3_character_max_results like `abc` becomes count 'abc'. 'abc' <= 0 and best.length < 'abc' are both false, so CharacterColorService.ts:351 reads best[-1].distance and throws a TypeError. This is the exact corruption route BUG-056's comment names.

No input reaches this: api-worker pickItem (resolver.ts:93-122) excludes primary.rowId from `chosen` and adds only sorted.slice(1), and a single XIVAPI search page has unique row_ids. The cited line is also wrong: chara-twins.ts is 165 lines and charaTwinsOf is at :71. It is a latent hypothetical, not a behaviour a test fails to pin.

title: PaletteService kMeansClustering caps k at pixel count, so images with fewer distinct colours than colorCount return duplicate 0-pixel clusters that discord /extractor renders as rows
reason: Once every distinct colour is a centroid, k-means++ :166-168 picks a duplicate pixel. Strict < in assignToClusters gives the clone 0 pixels and updateCentroids keeps it. discord extractor.ts:525-556 has no pixelCount filter: dedupe swaps each clone to a 'next best' dye, bandSlices gives it 7px, and the count inflates. web-app filters it and documents this exact case at extractor-tool.ts:2145-2158.

title: DyeSearch.test.ts findClosestDye/findDyesWithinDistance tests pass on null or empty results
reason: Vacuous on null or empty: toBeDefined + optional chain (:310-336), unguarded if (:510, :631), Array.isArray-only (:637-645). Misread: limit:0 (:515-522) asserts toBeGreaterThan(0), a real check. 3-digit hex is supported (normalizeHexKey :199), so nothing is hidden today.

title: DyeService.searchByLocalizedName returns all 125 dyes for an empty or whitespace query when the locale is loaded
reason: An empty or whitespace query folds to '' at :350, and every nameLower.includes('') is true. searchByName (DyeSearch.ts:83-89) returns []. Latent: the only caller, api-worker routes/dyes.ts:51, rejects an empty or whitespace q. foldForSearch keeps a leading combining mark, so no non-empty trimmed query folds to ''.

title: DyeDatabase.initialize accepts an all-invalid payload as a loaded empty DB, and duplicate ids only log through the NoOp logger
reason: The empty check :186-190 runs before the isValidDye filter :286; nothing re-checks afterwards, and isLoaded=true at :384. The duplicate id at :325-329 only calls logger.error despite its 'Fail loudly' comment. Latent: every caller passes the bundled dyeDatabase, which dye-vocabulary.test.ts guards. DEAD-047 (KEEP) covers the hue index, not :325.

title: dyes.json English name 'Opo-Opo Brown' disagrees with en.json/dyenames.csv 'Opo-opo Brown' (stainID 24, itemID 5752)
reason: A node comparison of dyes.json name vs en.json dyeNames[legacyItemID] finds 1 of 125 mismatches: stainID 24 (the claim said 20), itemID 5752. The CSV's English column comes from XIVAPI (scripts/README.md:28), so dyes.json is the outlier. Cosmetic: casing differs between dye.name and the localized en name.

title: build-locales.ts writes locale JSONs before exiting 1 on missing cells, and never checks dyes.json ids against dyenames.csv rows
reason: The write loop :114-133 runs before the missingCells exit at :138-152. buildDyeNames (:319-333) iterates CSV rows only. No script line or test cross-checks dyes.json ids (only a comment at :94). The only locale test spot-checks 2 ids (LocaleLoader.test.ts:88-89). Dev-tooling, defended at runtime by the English fallback.

title: APIService.getPriceData drops the pending entry before the async cache write
reason: The ordering is real, but the repro path has no in-repo caller. The only hit is the web-app wrapper at api-service-wrapper.ts:258, which DEAD-020 marks test-only. web-app prices go through getPricesForDataCenter (market-board-service.ts:353). title: PaletteService k-means++ uses Math.random, so palettes vary between runs
reason: Decided trade-off: extractor-tool.ts:451-456 documents random seeding and re-extracts only on a colour-count change. Standard k-means++ randomness gives valid palettes; no determinism contract exists. This is a feature request, not a defect.

title: gradient.ts ROW_WIDTHS.lead=28 ellipsises two-digit merged step ranges ('9–10' -> '9–…', '10–12' -> '10…')
reason: The lead is drawn via frame.ts:570 fitText(lead, 28, 13, 'mono'), which is 8.06 px per char (base.ts:310, factor 0.62). bot-logic gradient.ts:310 builds `${start}–${end}` and steps go up to 12 (schemas.ts:400). title: glamour-card.ts look label drawn at 10.5 px, below the documented 11 px type floor
reason: glamour-card.ts:237-239 draws lookLabel with `size: 10.5`, and :211 measures it at 10.5. frame.ts:10 and svg CLAUDE.md:21 both say 'Nothing below 11, ever'. No documented exception exists in docs or CLAUDE.md, and no other svg source goes below 11.

title: frame-budget.test.ts type-floor/text-extent gate omits glamour, swatch, a11y, dye-info and budget-ledger cards
reason: frame-budget.test.ts:28-35 imports only harmony, gradient, mixer, palette, nearest, random, contrast and comparison. The five other card families get only height<=350 or literal-size checks (swatch-card.test.ts:133, svg-pipeline.integration.test.ts). svg-02's live 10.5 px label proves the gap lets a floor violation ship.

title: contrast-card.ts tone/tier judged on the raw ratio while 13C·1 prints it rounded to 1 dp (2.96 shows '3.0' in failing red)
reason: ratioTier (:106-111) uses raw >=7/4.5/3. render13C1 prints num(p.ratio, lang, 1) (:427) in ratioTone(p.ratio) (:414), so 2.96 prints '3.0' in the tier-0 tone and 6.96 prints '7.0' in the tier-2 tone. The tier is WCAG-correct (no rounding), but the printed figure contradicts it. 13A/13B have the same edge at 2 dp (2.996 prints '3.00').

title: budget-calculator.ts mirrors the svg ledger geometry with literals (350-43-27, 24, 40, 32, 47) instead of the exported LEDGER_* constants
reason: Calculator :52-56 hardcodes the six numbers that budget-ledger.ts:107-116 owns. It uses them at :235/:243 to pack rows. Four of the constants are already exported from the barrel (index.ts:207-215) and go unused. GROUP_H and ROW_H barrel re-exports were removed by the earlier DEAD-015 because nothing imported them. Nothing tests parity.

title: emitted-glyphs.ts scanner fails open on \u escapes in literals and on a keyword-preceded regex (return /'/)
reason: Inside a literal, :141-143 skips every backslash pair, so '★' records nothing.
